problem.title: Large-scale document classification
problem.context: An insurer receives between two and eight million documents a day (scanned forms, e-mails, PDFs) and classifies each one into one of 60 claim types with an LLM-based classifier. Volume varies strongly over the year: storm season brings four times the usual load. Three teams use the results: claims handling, fraud investigation and analytics. The documents contain personal data.

requirements.text: Classify every incoming document into a claim type, with a confidence.
Deliver the results to the three consuming teams.
Send the documents the classifier is unsure about to human review, and use the reviewers' corrections to improve the classifier.
During storm season, at eight million documents a day, every document is classified within two hours of arrival.
When classification quality drops for one claim type (for example, after a form changes its layout), operators see it within one day.
The classification costs less than 0.2 cents per document on average over the year.
A consuming team can change how it processes the results without the other teams or the classifier having to change.
The documents contain personal data and may not leave the EU.
The classifier uses an LLM from the insurer's approved provider, in its EU region.

trajectory.hypothesis: The solution's choices together provide classification, delivery, review and monitoring while meeting throughput, cost, privacy and coupling requirements.
trajectory.observation: The design directly supports the functional requirements and names EU storage and an EU model region, but does not specify the locations of Kafka or the classifier service. Backlog scaling and batching plausibly help throughput and cost, but no measured capacity, latency or price establishes Q1 or Q3. Per-type dashboard metrics and weekly review-rate alerts help operators spot changes, but the specified weekly trigger does not establish detection within one day for every quality drop.

trajectory.hypothesis: R1, Q1, Q3 and C2 explain the approved model and a classifier path designed for peak throughput and lower per-document inference cost.
trajectory.observation: The regional approved LLM addresses C2, and the prompt describes all claim types and asks for a confidence, addressing R1. Batching and backlog scaling are plausible responses to volume and cost, but the solution gives no benchmark or cost figures to show the two-hour or annual cost thresholds are achieved.

trajectory.hypothesis: Does Q1 require backlog-based scaling, or could a fixed pool sized to peak volume suffice?
trajectory.observation: A fixed pool provisioned for peak load could meet the deadline, although it may spend more at ordinary volumes. The requirements support capacity for the peak but do not force backlog-based scaling; that scaling choice is free. The actual two-hour and cost targets remain unverified.

trajectory.hypothesis: R2 and Q4 explain publishing results to a shared stream with independent consumption by each team.
trajectory.observation: The topic serves all three teams, and separate consumer groups allow each to read at its own pace without coordinating changes to the classifier or the other consumers. The hourly warehouse load is an analytics-specific delivery path.

values: Result delivery: Kafka results topic

trajectory.hypothesis: Would a shared consumer group still deliver every result independently to all three teams as R2 and Q4 require?
trajectory.observation: A shared group normally distributes each message to one consumer in that group, rather than giving each team its own full stream. Separate groups are therefore required by this Kafka delivery arrangement to meet R2 and Q4.

trajectory.hypothesis: R3 explains routing uncertain predictions to people and using their corrections to improve the prompt safely.
trajectory.observation: Staff correct low-confidence cases, and those corrections feed monthly example updates that are checked against reviewed cases before release. R3 calls for review and learning, but does not prescribe 0.7, monthly cadence, prompt examples or a 2,000-document check; those implementation choices are free.

trajectory.hypothesis: Q2 explains per-type monitoring and sampling so operators can see quality changes.
trajectory.observation: Per-type metrics and human sampling can reveal deterioration, but the alert is based on a week-to-week doubling of review share. A quality drop may not double that measure, and the weekly cadence does not guarantee visibility within one day. This region helps observability but does not fully establish Q2.

alternatives.name: Document classification as built
alternatives.summary: An EU based event pipeline classifies documents through the approved LLM, distributes results through Kafka, routes uncertain cases to staff and monitors per-type quality.

choices.reason: The documents must remain in the EU; using EU object storage satisfies that location constraint.
choices.solution_quote: Incoming documents land in an object storage bucket in the EU region

choices.reason: An event enables asynchronous processing under variable load, but the requirements do not require Kafka specifically.
choices.solution_quote: each upload puts a message on a Kafka topic

choices.value_id: Text preparation: OCR, content-hash deduplication and adjacent text
choices.reason: OCR makes scanned inputs usable and deduplication can avoid repeat work; these techniques and the placement of extracted text are not prescribed.
choices.solution_quote: A preprocessing service reads the topic, extracts the text (with OCR for scanned forms), removes duplicates by content hash and writes the text next to the document.

choices.reason: The service provides a place to run the classifier, but Kubernetes is an implementation choice; peak capacity still needs evidence.
choices.solution_quote: A classifier service, running on Kubernetes

choices.value_id: LLM location: approved provider EU region
choices.reason: The approved provider and EU region are explicit constraints for processing personal documents.
choices.solution_quote: sends the text to the approved provider's LLM in its EU region.

choices.value_id: Prompt construction: 60 types with definitions and ten labelled examples
choices.reason: Listing the complete label set and requesting a confidence addresses classification, but definitions and ten examples per prompt are design choices.
choices.solution_quote: The prompt lists the 60 claim types with a short definition and ten labelled examples, and asks for a claim type and a confidence between 0 and 1.

choices.value_id: Inference batching: batches of 20 small documents
choices.reason: Batching is intended to reduce cost and can increase throughput, but no measured result establishes either target and the batch size is discretionary.
choices.solution_quote: Small documents are sent in batches of 20 to reduce cost.

choices.value_id: Worker scaling: backlog-based scaling from 4 to 120
choices.reason: A peak-sized fixed pool could meet the throughput deadline, so backlog-based scaling is a free way to respond to variable demand; the two-hour target remains unverified.
choices.solution_quote: The number of classifier workers scales with the length of the Kafka topic's backlog, from 4 to 120.

choices.value_id: Result provenance: prompt version and model stored with result
choices.reason: Recording model and prompt versions can help diagnose changes, but the requirements do not mandate this metadata.
choices.solution_quote: Every result is stored with the prompt version and the model name that produced it.

choices.reason: A topic decouples production from consumption, but Kafka is not the only way to distribute results.
choices.solution_quote: Results go to a second Kafka topic.

choices.value_id: Consumer isolation: separate consumer group per team
choices.reason: In this Kafka arrangement each team needs its own full stream; the contrast with a shared group would divide messages among teams. The general requirement does not mandate Kafka itself.
choices.solution_quote: Each consuming team has its own consumer group and reads at its own pace

choices.reason: This serves analytics, but neither a warehouse nor hourly loading is specified by the requirement.
choices.solution_quote: analytics also loads the topic into the data warehouse every hour.

choices.value_id: Review routing: confidence-below-0.7 queue with staff correction
choices.reason: Human review of uncertain predictions is required. The 0.7 threshold and queue implementation are free choices.
choices.solution_quote: Documents with a confidence below 0.7 go to a review queue in a labelling tool, where claims staff correct the claim type.

choices.value_id: Feedback cadence: monthly replacement with recent corrections
choices.reason: Using corrections to improve the classifier is required, while monthly prompt-example replacement is one chosen update method and cadence.
choices.solution_quote: Every month the team replaces the prompt's examples with recent corrected documents

choices.value_id: Prompt validation: 2,000 reviewed documents before switching
choices.reason: Checking a proposed change against labelled cases can reduce regression risk, but this sample size and gate are not prescribed.
choices.solution_quote: and checks the new prompt against 2,000 reviewed documents before switching to it.

choices.value_id: Drift monitoring: per-type review share and mean confidence dashboard
choices.reason: Per-type indicators make changes visible, but the requirement does not specify these metrics or a dashboard.
choices.solution_quote: A dashboard shows, per claim type, the share of documents sent to review and the mean confidence

choices.value_id: Alerting: alert on doubled weekly review share
choices.reason: An alert supports detection, but the chosen signal and threshold may miss quality drops and do not guarantee one-day visibility.
choices.solution_quote: an alert fires when the share sent to review for a claim type doubles from one week to the next.

choices.value_id: Quality audit: weekly random sample of 300
choices.reason: Human review of a random sample offers another quality signal, but the frequency and sample size are choices and weekly sampling alone cannot ensure the one-day target.
choices.solution_quote: Each week, analysts review a random sample of 300 classified documents.

adrs.title: Keep document processing in the approved EU environment
adrs.context: Documents contain personal data and may not leave the EU, and inference must use the insurer's approved provider in its EU region.

values: Document storage: EU object storage
LLM location: approved provider EU region
pros: Meets the explicit data-location and provider constraints.
cons: The constraints limit storage and model-location choices.
options.reason: The EU location and approved provider are forced by C1 and C2.

adrs.title: Prepare and classify documents through an elastic inference path
adrs.context: Every document needs a claim type and confidence, while storm-season volume creates a demanding deadline and average cost ceiling.

options.name: Preprocess, batch and scale the approved classifier
values: Ingestion notification: Kafka upload event
Text preparation: OCR, content-hash deduplication and adjacent text
Classifier runtime: Kubernetes service
Prompt construction: 60 types with definitions and ten labelled examples
Inference batching: batches of 20 small documents
Worker scaling: backlog-based scaling from 4 to 120
pros: Handles scanned inputs and provides a prompt covering the full label set.
Batching and backlog scaling respond to variable volume and may reduce per-document cost.
cons: No benchmark establishes classification within two hours at peak load.
No cost accounting establishes the annual cost ceiling.
options.reason: R1 calls for classifying documents, but the runtime, prompt details, batching and scaling method are implementation choices. Batching and backlog scaling are plausible for Q1 and Q3, which remain unproven by the supplied design.

options.name: Fixed peak-capacity worker pool
values: Classifier runtime: Kubernetes service
LLM location: approved provider EU region
Prompt construction: 60 types with definitions and ten labelled examples
Inference batching: batches of 20 small documents
Worker scaling: fixed worker capacity
pros: Can meet the peak deadline if provisioned for the required capacity.
cons: May leave expensive capacity idle outside storm season.
options.reason: A fixed pool could satisfy the peak requirement if sized correctly, so backlog scaling is not forced; this option was not selected.

adrs.title: Distribute each result to independently operating teams
adrs.context: All three consuming teams need results, and one team's processing changes should not require changes by the other teams or the classifier.

options.name: Shared topic with per-team consumer groups
values: Result delivery: Kafka results topic
Consumer isolation: separate consumer group per team
Analytics delivery: hourly warehouse load
pros: Each team can consume the full stream at its own pace.
The classifier does not need to coordinate downstream processing changes.
cons: Kafka and hourly warehouse loading are specific implementation choices.
options.reason: Independent result access is required for these three teams, but Kafka is free. Separate groups are the required isolation arrangement once this Kafka design is chosen.

options.name: Shared consumer group
values: Result delivery: Kafka results topic
Consumer isolation: shared consumer group
pros: Shares the work among consumers in a group.
cons: Each message is generally handled by only one group member, so every team would not receive every result.
options.reason: This does not meet delivery to all teams or their independent processing needs.

adrs.title: Use human corrections to improve classification
adrs.context: Cases the classifier is unsure about need human review, and corrections must feed back into classifier improvement.

options.name: Review low-confidence cases and validate monthly prompt updates
values: Review routing: confidence-below-0.7 queue with staff correction
Feedback cadence: monthly replacement with recent corrections
Prompt validation: 2,000 reviewed documents before switching
pros: Staff corrections address uncertain cases and provide fresh examples.
Validation checks the updated prompt before it is used.
cons: A fixed threshold can send some useful cases to review or leave uncertain cases automated.
Monthly updates limit how quickly corrections change the prompt.
options.reason: Human review and using corrections are forced by R3. The threshold, monthly schedule, prompt update method and validation set are free implementation choices.

adrs.title: Monitor classification quality by claim type
adrs.context: Operators should see a quality drop for an individual claim type within one day.

options.name: Per-type dashboard, weekly review-rate alert and sample audit
values: Result provenance: prompt version and model stored with result
Drift monitoring: per-type review share and mean confidence dashboard
Alerting: alert on doubled weekly review share
Quality audit: weekly random sample of 300
pros: Per-type metrics and model/prompt provenance aid diagnosis.
The sample audit can expose problems that aggregate automated metrics miss.
cons: A weekly rate comparison may not reveal a quality drop within one day.
A quality drop need not double the share sent to review.
options.reason: These signals support Q2, but their cadence and trigger do not establish the required one-day detection. The specific monitoring choices are free, and Q2 is only partly addressed.
